case_name: Anil Kumar & Ors v. The State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Anil Kumar & Ors — husband, wife, and others
parties.respondent_defendant: The State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr — government and another respondent

facts_of_case: Marriage between petitioner no.1 and respondent No.2 was solemnized in 2005. Due to matrimonial differences, they started living separately since 2013. In 2015, respondent No.2 filed a petition under Section 125 Cr.P.C. against the petitioner No.1. The matter was settled between the parties by way of settlement before the Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi in 2020.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle disputes through mediation and such settlements are enforceable.
legal_principles.held: In lieu of such settlement, now petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 are residing together in the matrimonial house.

legal_principles.principle: A settlement agreement can supersede pending legal proceedings.
legal_principles.held: In lieu of such settlement, now petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 are residing together in the matrimonial house.

outcome.final_order: FIR No.421/2015 under Section 498A/406/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Nihal Vihar, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
